newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela union calls for one-day strike Aug 6.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela union calls for one-day strike Aug 6.

text.p: Venezuela's largest union, the Confederation of Venezuelan Workers (CTV), said Wednesday it was calling for a one-day national strike on August 6 to protest domestic gasoline price hikes and tardy salary rises.
"We are calling for a national strike on August 6 between 6 a.m. and 7 p.m.," CTV Secretary General Carlos Navarro told Reuters in a brief telephone interview.

"We are in an emergency situation. We are protesting because the private sector has not given salary rises, because of the increase in gasoline prices and because of the (price) increase for basic services," Navarro added.
It would be the first national strike in Venezuela in eight years.
Domestic gasoline prices are due to increase by 27 percent at midnight Thursday and government officials have said private sector companies must raise wages to meet higher living costs.
Business chamber leaders have said that they have already raised salaries, and criticized the union's strike call.
"This will not contribute to bringing social peace to the country," Henrique Ball, president of industrial chamber Conindustria, told Radio Caracas Radio.
Navarro said the decision to call for a strike had been taken at a meeting of all of Venezuela's major unions.
Union leaders have complained that private sector wages have not been increased as had been agreed under a labor law reform hammered out between government, business and union leaders two months ago.
Ball insisted that 90 percent of his chamber's members had already increased employee salaries.
Government ministers were expected to discuss how best to resolve the dispute over salary increases at a weekly cabinet meeting Wednesday afternoon.
Labor Minister Mara Bernadoni said Tuesday the government had not ruled out forcing the private sector to raise wages by decree.
